findings.explanation: Tagging resources is not enough: a user-defined tag only appears as a `resourceTags/user:*` column in the CUR after it is activated as a cost allocation tag in the Billing console, and only from activation onward. Without that step every row lands in `untagged`.
findings.quote: Requires tags on resources generating egress; untagged flows appear as `untagged`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: activate the `Application` tag as a user-defined cost allocation tag in AWS Billing and Cost Management (management/payer account), enable 'Include resource IDs' on the CUR, and note that tag values are not back-filled before activation; the column surfaces in Splunk as `resourceTags_user_Application`.

findings.explanation: The SPL attributes only EC2-product data transfer, yet the title, `implementation` and `visualization` ('egress by tag') present it as data-transfer attribution in general. Transfer billed under other product codes (S3, RDS, CloudFront, etc.) is excluded, and the `*Bytes*` wildcard also pulls in NAT Gateway processing (`NatGateway-Bytes`) and zero-cost `*-In-Bytes` lines.
findings.suggested_fix: State in `description` and `implementation` that the report covers EC2 data-transfer and NAT-processing usage types only (e.g. `*-DataTransfer-Out-Bytes`, `*-DataTransfer-Regional-Bytes`, `*-AWS-Out-Bytes`), and point to sibling UC-20.1.8 / UC-20.1.25 for other services and NAT egress.

findings.explanation: The SPL has no `span` and no threshold; it is a sorted attribution report, so alert-style false positives (maintenance windows, synthetic probes, batch jobs) do not apply. The real accuracy issues for this report are mis-attribution: untagged or inconsistently cased tag values, tags activated mid-period, and shared resources (NAT gateways, load balancers) whose transfer lands on one tag.
findings.quote: Planned work for 'Data Transfer Cost Attribution by Tag' shifts `xfer_cost` over `span=1h`
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with attribution caveats: tag-value drift (e.g. 'Payments' vs 'payments'), costs before tag activation reported as untagged, shared-infrastructure transfer attributed to the owner of the ENI/instance, and in-bytes rows that carry zero cost.

findings.explanation: The duplicated generic Steps 1–5 treat this chargeback report as a paging alert with 5–15 minute polling, vendor 'inventory count' validation and HEC troubleshooting. CUR lands in S3 a few times a day, and chargeback is normally run per billing month, so a 24-hour window and per-entity throttling are wrong guidance.
findings.quote: Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the generic block. Run the report per billing period (e.g. month-to-date and last full month), schedule it daily after the CUR refresh, and validate totals against Cost Explorer filtered to Usage Type Group 'EC2: Data Transfer' for the same accounts and dates.

findings.explanation: 'CUR with resource tags' is a data source, not an app; it also leaks into `detailedImplementation` as 'Install and configure the required add-on or app: CUR with resource tags.'
findings.quote: CUR with resource tags — Splunk Add-on for Amazon Web Services (Splunkbase 1876)
findings.suggested_fix: App: Splunk Add-on for Amazon Web Services (Splunkbase 1876), 'Billing (Cost and Usage Report)' input. Move 'CUR with resource tags' to `dataSources`.

findings.explanation: The UC reads AWS CUR data only; tagging it as Splunk equipment is inconsistent with sibling AWS cost UCs (e.g. UC-20.1.2 uses `aws`).
HEC and inputs.conf are generic and not used by this CUR input; the references a reader actually needs (CUR data-transfer usage types, cost allocation tag activation) are missing.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `lineItem_UsageType="*Bytes*"` also matches `NatGateway-Bytes` (NAT data processing, not transfer) and zero-charge `*-In-Bytes` rows; consider explicit transfer usage-type patterns, and optionally filter `lineItem_LineItemType` to usage rows so credits/discounts do not skew per-app totals.

summary: The SPL is a reasonable EC2 data-transfer chargeback report on CUR, but the text never says it is EC2-only, omits the essential cost-allocation-tag activation step, and wraps a ranking report in generic alerting, false-positive and troubleshooting boilerplate that does not fit it.
